Onkar Singh on 13 May, 2014 In The Court Of Ms. Ravinder Bedi : Presiding Officer, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal : Karkardooma Courts : East District : Delhi Mac Petition No: 334/11 Unique Case Id No: 02402C0317742011 Ms. Neetu Mahana D/o Sh. texts.facts: The petitioner has filed present claim under section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ (Rupees Ten Lac only) for the injuries suffered by her in the accident dated 19.03.2005. 2. The case of the petitioner is that on 19.03.2005 at about 3.30 PM, she was travelling in Bus bearing No. DL1PA3485 and was proceeding to her house after taking class. When the bus reached near Heera Sweets, Shakarpur, its right rear tyre suddenly burst with explosion, also Ms. Neetu Mahana D/O Sh. Parvesh Kumar vs Sh. Mahesh Kumar S/O Sh. Onkar Singh on 13 May, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101567846/ 1 exploding and dismantling the basemetal seat of the bus floor. The petitioner, who was sitting just above the basemetal seat, received grievous injuries and was immediately taken to the Walia Nursing Home where her MLC No.943/05 was prepared. Later, she was shifted to GTB Hospital, Dilshad Garden, Delhi on account of her precarious condition. 3. The respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner and respondent no.3 is the insurer of the bus. 4. The notice of petition was served upon all the respondents. The MAC Petition No: 334/11 Page No: 2/12 respondents no. 1 and 2 filed their separate written statements in which the allegations in the petition are denied. In entire written statement, the contents of the petition are denied simplicitor. The respondent no.3/Insurance company filed written statement admitting that vehicle no. DL1PA3485 was insured with respondent no.3 from 08.11.2004 to 07.11.2005 in the name of respondent no.2; that the respondent no.3 has taken all the defences available under law U/s 147, 149 and 170 of the M.V. Act. 5. On the basis of the pleadings, following issues were framed by Ld. Predecessor on 01.03.2013 : 1. Whether the petitioner has suffered injuries in road side accident on 19.03.05 involving vehicle i.e. DTC bus bearing registration No. DL1PA3485 being driven allegedly in a rash and negligent manner by respondent no.1? 2. 3. Relief. 6. The petitioner has examined herself as PW1 and has relied upon the documents i.e. treatment record as Ex.PW1/1 (colly.), medical bills amounting to Rs.2,954/ as Ex.PW1/2 (colly.), criminal case record as Ex.PW1/3, ration card Ex.PW1/4, certificate dated 3.9.2004 issued by Rehabilitation Unit of Audiology & Speed MAC Petition No: 334/11 Page No: 3/12 Pathology Department as Ex.PW1/5, copy of her Identity Card for the disabled as Ex.PW1/6 (colly.), Election I card and Aadhar Card as Mark A and B. Petitioner has also examined Sh. Shekhar Anand, Record Clerk, GTB Hospital as PW2 who has proved the treatment record Ex.PW2/A (colly.). PW3 Sh. Pravesh Kumar, petitioner's father has proved educational qualification certificates of petitioner as Ex.PW3/A (colly.). The respondents however have not led contra evidence. When the bus reached near Heera MAC Petition No: 334/11 Page No: 4/12 Sweets, Shakarpur, the right rear tyre of the said bus suddenly burst with explosion, damaging the basemetal seat of the bus floor. The petitioner, who was sitting just above the basemetal seat, received grievous injuries.
texts.arguments: Counsel for respondent no.3 contended that there was neither rashness nor negligence in driving of the offending vehicle and the injuries suffered by petitioner cannot be attributable to the rashness or negligence of the driver. In this context, I am placing reliance upon the judgment in Kaushnuma Begum & Ors. Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., I (2001) ACC 151 (SC). In the process of capsizing, it hit against a pedestrian, who was walking on the road at that ill fated moment and consequently was crushed and subsequently succumbed to injuries. Hon'ble Apex Court observed that the compensation on account of accident arising from use of motor vehicles can be claimed under the common law even without the aid of a Statute. In Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors.1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Guwahati High Court has observed as under : "In deciding a matter, tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case. In a criminal case in order to have conviction, the matter is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt and in a civil case the matter is to be decided on the basis of preponderance of evidence, but in a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in a civil case. After all, it is a summary inquiry and this is a legislation for the welfare of the society." 11.This case was noticed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case titled as Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Ms. Neetu Mahana D/O Sh. Parvesh Kumar vs Sh. Mahesh Kumar S/O Sh. Onkar Singh on 13 May, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101567846/ 3 MAC Petition No: 334/11 Page No: 6/12 Kamlesh : 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310 where adverse inference was drawn because the driver of the offending vehicle had not appeared in the witness box to corroborate his defence taken in the written statement. It was noted that there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in the case. 12.In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr., MANU/SC/ 1018/2010, Civil Appeal No. 8981/2010 decided on 18.10.2010, following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims: i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner. In Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. v. Lalita, AIR 1981 Delhi 558, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that there cannot be any deduction if domestic help is obtained from a family member. The Hon'ble High Court has observed as under : "...........A wrong doer cannot take advantage of this 'domestic element'. If the mother renders service to her, instead of a nurse, it is right and just that she should recover compensation for the value of the services that the mother has rendered to her. Mother's services were necessitated by the wrong doing and the injured should be compensated for it. (Cunnigharn v. Harrison 3 All E.R. 463). The services of a wife and mother are worth more than those of a house keeper because she is in constant attendance and does many more things than a housekeeper. (Regan v. Williamson (1976) 2 All E.R. 241)." This judgment was again relied upon by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Narayan Bahadur v. Sumeet Gupta and Anr., MAC APP.No.762/11 dated 04.07.12. 18. , in that event, in the light of the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Kashmiri Lal, 2007 ACJ 688
